Voici le rapport verbatim renvoyé par le subagent `ux-designer` : --- ## Audit Report — `tools/bench-agent-cost/fixtures/design_target.html` ### Summary Read-only WCAG 2.2 AA + Nielsen heuristic audit of a synthetic "Account Settings" email-update form. Four violations are deliberately planted per the file's own header comment; one of those four is misattributed in the comment itself and I report the technically correct citation below rather than the comment's label (zetetic standard: verify the claim, don't repeat it). Two additional heuristic-level findings surfaced during the mandatory 10-heuristic walk are reported separately. ### User and task (Move 1) - User segment: returning authenticated account holder, plus a screen-reader/keyboard-only user updating account email; competency: has an account, no assumed accessibility-tool expertise. - Task: update the account email address and receive confirmation of validity/save. - Success criterion: form field reachable and operable via keyboard and screen reader; validation errors announced and diagnosable; save action reachable by all input modalities. - Failure modes covered by this audit: label lost on input (AT users get no field name), error not announced to AT, primary action unreachable by keyboard/AT, icon-only control untappable/unlabeled. ### Stakes classification - Classification: **Medium-High** — account/credential-adjacent form (email is typically a recovery/auth channel); not a checkout flow but failure here can lock a user out of account recovery. Full Moves 1–3, 5 applied; Move 4 (IA) not applicable (single-field surface, <10 destinations). ### Severity scale used Not prescribed verbatim by `agents/ux-designer.md` or `skills/design/design.md`, so I adopt the WCAG-conformance-anchored scale standard in industry audits (Deque/WebAIM convention): **Blocker** = Level A failure that fully prevents task completion for an entire user group; **Critical** = Level A/AA failure that severely impairs completion or removes essential information; **Major** = Level AA failure that degrades usability without full blockage; **Minor** = below-AA/best-practice gap. --- ### Violations found | # | Element | Criterion | Severity | Minimal fix | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | `` (line 13) | **WCAG 2.2 — 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions** (Level A). Placeholder is the only name cue; it disappears on input, and per WCAG's accname spec a placeholder is a weak, non-persistent substitute for a label. Compounds into **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (Level A) risk if the placeholder is later removed/changed at runtime. | **Blocker** — screen-reader users get no persistent field identity once focused or once text is entered; sighted users lose the cue mid-task. | Add `` and `id="email"` on the input; keep the placeholder only as a supplementary format hint, never the sole label. | | B | `Invalid format` (line 17) | **Corrected finding — not 1.4.1 as the file's own comment claims.** The span carries the word "Invalid format" as text, so color is *not* the sole conveyor of the error (1.4.1 is technically satisfied here). The real defect is **WCAG 2.2 — 1.3.1 Info and Relationships** (Level A) and **3.3.1 Error Identification** (Level A): the error text has no `id`, is not referenced by the input via `aria-describedby`, and carries no `role="alert"`/`aria-live` region, so a screen-reader user tabbed to the email field, or present when the error appears dynamically, is never told the field is in error or why (also implicates **4.1.3 Status Messages**, Level AA, for the dynamic-insertion case). | **Critical** — the error is fully invisible to assistive technology despite being visible to sighted users, i.e., a strictly worse gap than plain color-only encoding. | Give the span `id="email-error" role="alert"`, and add `aria-describedby="email-error" aria-invalid="true"` to the input when the error is present. Pair with an icon for scanability, but the core fix is programmatic association, not color. | | C | `
Save changes
` (lines 22–24) | **WCAG 2.2 — 2.1.1 Keyboard** (Level A): no `tabindex`, no keydown handler — unreachable and unactivatable from a keyboard. **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (Level A): no `role="button"`, so assistive technology cannot expose it as an actionable control at all — it is exposed as inert text. Consequently **2.4.7 Focus Visible** (Level AA) is moot because the element is never focusable. | **Blocker** — this is the form's only submit action; keyboard-only and screen-reader users cannot complete the task at all. | Replace with a native ``. | | D | `` (lines 28–30) | Two independent violations on one element: **WCAG 2.2 — 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)** (Level AA) — 16×16 CSS px is below the 24×24 px floor. **WCAG 2.2 — 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value** (Level A) — `aria-label=""` is an explicit empty string, which wins the accessible-name computation over the `×` text content, so the button's accessible name is empty; a screen reader announces only "button" with no purpose. | **Critical** (name) + **Major** (size) | Remove the empty `aria-label=""` (or set it to a real value, e.g. `aria-label="Close"`) and increase the hit target to at least 24×24 CSS px. | ### Additional heuristic findings (non-planted, surfaced by the mandated 10-heuristic walk) | Heuristic | Pass/Fail | Evidence / fix | |---|---|---| | 1. Visibility of system status | Fail | No visual state change on the `` itself when validation fails — only the disconnected span at line 17 changes. Add a visible error state tied to the same fix as Violation B. | | 9. Help recognize/diagnose/recover from errors | Fail | "Invalid format" names the problem but gives no example of the expected format or next action.
